questions.q: What are the four pillars of greatness in the book?
a: The self, the story, the philosophy and the team
Strategy, finance, marketing and operations
Vision, funding, product and sales
Knowledge, skills, network and reputation
questions.why: Lesson 1 groups Bartlett's laws under the self, the story, the philosophy and the team.

questions.q: In what order does Bartlett say you should fill your five career buckets?
a: Knowledge, skills, network, resources and reputation
Reputation, network, skills, knowledge and resources
Skills, knowledge, resources, reputation and network
Network, resources, reputation, knowledge and skills
questions.why: Lesson 2 says each bucket grows the next, so knowledge comes first, then skills, network, resources and reputation.

questions.q: What does the rule never become wallpaper mean?
a: Stand out rather than blend into what people tune out
Decorate your workspace to inspire your team
Keep your brand colors consistent everywhere
Change your strategy with every new trend
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains wallpaper as the things we ignore because we see them so often.

questions.q: Why does Bartlett advise being an inconsistent leader?
a: Different people have different needs and need different treatment
Consistency is impossible once a team grows large
Rules should change every week to keep people alert
Leaders should favor their most loyal employees
questions.why: Lesson 2 says treating everyone the same leaves some people unhappy because their needs differ.

questions.q: What is the point of Bartlett's final law, learning never ends?
a: Making learning a habit keeps you growing as a founder
Formal education is the only path to success
Reading one book a year is enough for any CEO
Experience matters more than any new knowledge
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the most useful principle is the one you have not discovered yet, so keep learning.
